cards.operation: Consolidate an equivalent repeated caveat while retaining its scope and a clear surviving statement.
steps: Find two caveats about the same subject and evidential boundary.
Keep the full caveat in the section where its scope is clearest.
Shorten only the redundant occurrence and retain its attribution.
preserve: At least one explicit statement of each distinct evidential boundary
counterexamples: Combining limitations of different methods merely because both say untested
Removing all reminders that the study has not been conducted
cards.review_notes: A scope-equivalent caveat survived in another section; literal keyword overlap alone is insufficient.

conditions.text: Find two caveats about the same subject and evidential boundary.
Caveats concern different claims or sources
Only one statement preserves the uncertainty or untested status
Removing the caveat would make its local claim unconditional

payload.label: associated_success
payload.before: Selecting evidence before rewriting adapts the attribution-first approach, while fine-grained checking draws on reference-based claim verification. Neither source establishes preservation during proposal revision [S2][S5].
payload.after: Evidence selection before rewriting adapts the attribution-first approach, and fine-grained checking draws on reference-based claim verification [S2][S5].
payload.retained_elsewhere: although neither study establishes that claim locks preserve research proposal content.

cards.operation: Make an already-stated assessment object and criterion relation explicit.
steps: Identify the object and criterion already present in the current target.
Express their existing comparison directly; do not invent how reviewers decide or add new criteria.
preserve: The original assessment object and criteria
counterexamples: Adding a scoring rubric or annotation procedure not in the draft
Mistaking a language model tool for the comparison standard
cards.review_notes: Source edit made the workflow-steps/task-requirements relation explicit without adding a new protocol. Vague-claim use is a reviewed engineering generalization.

conditions.text: Identify the object and criterion already present in the current target.
Using names a tool rather than a criterion
The intended comparison is ambiguous or already explicit

payload.label: associated_success
payload.before: Human reviewers will assess applicability using workflow steps and task requirements.
payload.after: Human reviewers will assess applicability by examining workflow steps against task requirements.

cards.operation: Lead with already-present concrete substance rather than broad framing.
steps: Locate a concrete neighboring statement in the same paragraph.
Move that existing substance ahead of broad framing without changing its qualifiers.
Retain the objective and all substantive constraints.
counterexamples: Inventing a failure mode to make the opening vivid
Presenting a hypothetical risk as an observed result
cards.review_notes: The observed source edit led with an existing risk. Applying the same role allocation to other concrete substance is an engineering generalization, not separately observed causal evidence. Its factual content must never transfer.

conditions.text: Locate a concrete neighboring statement in the same paragraph.
No concrete substance already exists in the same paragraph
The paragraph already leads with that substance

payload.label: associated_success
payload.before: Academic revision requires clearer expression without changes to supported claims, qualifiers, or citation relationships. Fluency alone does not meet this requirement: a rewrite can strengthen a tentative conclusion or disconnect a statement from its evidence.
payload.after: A fluent rewrite can strengthen a tentative conclusion or disconnect a statement from its evidence. Academic revision therefore requires attention to supported claims, qualifiers, and citation relationships as well as expression.

cards.operation: Replace a broad payoff statement with the concrete comparison already described in this draft.
steps: Use the supporting current passage to state what is being compared or inspected and what question that addresses.
Keep the statement prospective and retain its scope; merge rather than append another promise.
counterexamples: Inventing an experimental protocol to make a conclusion specific
Calling an expected benefit a finding
cards.review_notes: Both observed edits replace a general evaluation promise with a question linked to existing evaluation actions. Raw source content must not transfer.

conditions.text: Use the supporting current passage to state what is being compared or inspected and what question that addresses.
No related comparison is already present
The change requires a new procedure, threshold or result

payload.label: associated_success
payload.before: The proposed study will evaluate editing order as a constrained decision problem.
payload.after: By matching resources, assessing quality dimensions separately, and inspecting revision histories, the proposed study aims to identify when global revision should precede local editing and when another schedule may be preferable.

payload.label: associated_success
payload.before: The study can identify tradeoffs between harmful reuse, excessive abstention, and revision quality.
payload.after: By examining the revisions that follow reuse and abstention, the planned study will assess whether avoiding harmful reuse comes at the cost of withholding useful guidance or reducing revision quality.

cards.operation: Give repeated material distinct section roles instead of repeating the same operational statement.
steps: Compare only the shared proposition in the two current passages.
Keep the operational detail in Methodology or Experiments; let the overview state its already-supported purpose.
Retain every unique control, component, qualification and citation; skip ambiguous equivalence.
preserve: Unique details and conditions in both passages
counterexamples: Inventing new component interactions to replace an inventory
cards.style_countercondition: Do not replace repeated controls with synonyms or a longer explanation of the same controls. Change only the shared rhetorical role; retain every distinct condition.
cards.review_notes: The accepted source condensed a repeated inventory. Extending its section-role operation to other supported repeated propositions is an explicitly reviewed engineering generalization. The negative example is style-only association, not causation.

conditions.text: Compare only the shared proposition in the two current passages.
The target supplies a unique detail that cannot be retained
The passages concern different sources or claims

payload.label: associated_success
payload.before: We propose a memory schema recording detected style issues, editing procedures, applicability conditions, source identifiers, protected claims, and verification outcomes. Records would transfer procedures rather than factual assertions.
payload.after: The proposed memory would transfer editing procedures rather than factual assertions. Each procedure would remain tied to the context and verification judgments associated with its use, allowing later revisions to be assessed against their own evidence.
payload.retained_elsewhere: Each memory record would contain the detected issue, editing procedure, applicability conditions, source identifiers, protected claims, and verification outcomes.

payload.label: style_only_counterexample
payload.before: Answers, source pools, and candidate passages will remain fixed across conditions.
payload.after: Answers, source pools, and candidate passages will remain fixed across conditions so that differences in citation presentation can be assessed without attributing answer-content differences to selection policies.
